My name is Maria, and I lead a patient group supporting families affected by MPS IIIA (Sanfilippo syndrome type A). I am writing to introduce our group and to explore whether there might be an opportunity to work together.

AIMPS ETS was founded in 1991 to support children and adult patients affected by rare genetic metabolic diseases, including MPS IIIA, which often lead to severe disability [E080e178].

Since our two groups both support families living with MPS IIIA, I believe there could be real value in connecting, whether to share experiences, exchange resources, or simply learn from one another's approaches to supporting patients and families.

As a modest first step, would you be open to a short introductory call in the coming weeks to discuss our respective work and see where common ground might exist?

Thank you very much for considering this. I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Maria
Patient group leader

My name is Maria, and I lead a patient group supporting families affected by MPS IIIB (Sanfilippo syndrome type B). I am writing to introduce myself and explore a possible connection with your organisation.

I understand that AIMPS ETS was founded in 1991 to support children and adult patients affected by these rare genetic metabolic diseases, which often lead to severe disability [E994105e]. MPS IIIB is caused by deficiency of the lysosomal enzyme alpha-N-acetylglucosaminidase (NAGLU), leading to accumulation of heparan sulfate within lysosomes [Eac469c9][E4da5d49]. Given that your organisation's work spans this same disease area, I believe there may be valuable common ground between our communities, particularly around shared experiences of caring for families with these conditions.

I would be glad to arrange a short call, at your convenience, simply to learn more about your work and see whether there might be opportunities for our groups to share information or support one another going forward.

Thank you for considering this, and I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Maria
Patient Group Leader (MPS IIIB)

My name is Maria, and I lead a patient group for families affected by Mucopolysaccharidosis type IIIC (MPS IIIC).

A paper reports that AIMPS ETS was founded in 1991 to support children and adult patients affected by rare genetic metabolic diseases, including MPS IIIC, which often lead to severe disability [E30302cc]. A paper reports that MPS IIIC is caused by a deficiency of the lysosomal enzyme HGSNAT, resulting in storage of heparan sulfate in cells [E108a4c3][E7373ae4]. Since your organisation's founding mission already encompasses support for families living with MPS IIIC, I believe our groups may have complementary experience and contacts that could be valuable to share.

I would be glad to introduce our group more fully and hear about your current activities related to MPS IIIC. Would you be open to a short introductory call in the coming weeks to explore whether there are simple ways we could support one another?

Thank you for considering this, and for the work your organisation does for affected families.

Warm regards,
Maria
Patient Group Leader (MPS IIIC)

My name is Maria, and I lead a patient group for MPS IIID. I'm writing to introduce myself and explore whether we might collaborate.

A paper reports that AIMPS ETS was founded in 1991 to support children and adult patients affected by these rare genetic metabolic diseases, which often lead to severe disability [Ea6b3adc]. The same source indicates your organisation supports families affected by MPS IIIA, MPS IIIB, MPS IIIC, MPS I, and MPS II as well [E080e178][E994105e][E30302cc][E68fcb3d][Ebb059e1].

MPS IIID shares a closely related biological mechanism with these conditions: a paper reports that MPS IIID is caused by deficiency of the lysosomal enzyme N-acetylglucosamine 6-sulfatase, leading to accumulation of heparan sulfate [E9f300a9][Ef8f5811]. Similarly, a paper reports that MPS IIIA results from a deficient lysosomal enzyme causing defective degradation and storage of heparan sulfate [Ec586fdd][E8282821]. Given this overlap, I believe our communities could learn from each other's experience.

Would you be open to a short call in the coming weeks to share how our groups work and see where we might support one another?

Thank you for your time.

Warm regards,
Maria
Patient group leader, MPS IIID patient group

{"org_id": "ORG:AIMPS_ETS", "disease_id": "MONDO:0011758", "to": "info@aimps.it", "recipient_reason": "patient group linked to this disease (studies edge) with a general contact email", "subject": "Introduction and possible collaboration between our MPS patient groups", "body": "Dear AIMPS ETS,

I am Maria, a parent leading a patient group supporting families affected by MPS I (Hurler). I am writing to introduce our group and to explore whether a collaboration might be possible.

A paper reports that AIMPS ETS was founded in 1991 to support children and adult patients affected by these rare genetic metabolic diseases, which often lead to severe disability [E68fcb3d]. Your organisation's work spans MPS I (Hurler) as well as related conditions, including MPS II (Hunter), MPS IIIA, MPS IIIB, MPS IIIC and MPS IIID [E68fcb3d][Ebb059e1][E080e178][E994105e][E30302cc][Ea6b3adc].

A paper reports that MPS I (Hurler) is caused by deficiency of the enzyme alpha-L-iduronidase, leading to storage of dermatan and heparan sulfate [Ef4f70c3]. A paper reports that MPS II (Hunter), one of the conditions your organisation also supports, likewise involves accumulation of dermatan and heparan sulfate due to a different enzyme deficiency [E385b672]. Given these shared storage mechanisms across the MPS family, I believe our communities face many overlapping challenges and could learn from one another.

Would you be open to a short introductory call, perhaps 20-30 minutes, to share experiences and discuss how our groups might support each other going forward?

Thank you for your time, and I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Maria
Patient group leader

My name is Maria, and I lead a patient group for MPS II (Hunter syndrome). I am reaching out to introduce our group and explore a possible collaboration.

A paper reports that AIMPS ETS was founded in 1991 to support children and adult patients affected by rare genetic metabolic diseases that often cause serious disability, and lists MPS II among the conditions it serves [Ebb059e1]. The same source also lists MPS I (Hurler) [E68fcb3d] and the MPS III subtypes IIIA, IIIB, IIIC and IIID [E080e178][E994105e][E30302cc][Ea6b3adc] among the diseases AIMPS ETS supports. Papers report that MPS II and MPS I share overlapping biology, including storage of dermatan sulfate [E385b672][Ef4f70c3] and heparan sulfate [E1f3fa46][Ea90608d], arising from lysosomal enzyme deficiency [Ef5d5a50][E834d07e]. Given this shared underlying biology across the MPS family, I think our two groups could usefully exchange experience.

Would you be open to a brief introductory call in the coming weeks to discuss how our communities support families and where we might collaborate?

Thank you for your time, and I look forward to your reply.

Warm regards,
Maria
Patient group leader, MPS II (Hunter) patient group

{"org_id": "ORG:Asociación_MPS_LISOSOMALES_España", "disease_id": "MONDO:0009265", "to": "info@mpslisosomales.org", "recipient_reason": "patient group linked to this disease (studies edge) with a general contact email", "subject": "Proposing a connection between our lysosomal disease patient communities", "body": "Dear colleagues at Asociación MPS-LISOSOMALES España,

My name is Maria, and I lead a patient group supporting families affected by Gaucher disease.

I understand that your association works to raise awareness of lysosomal diseases such as Mucopolysaccharidosis, Fabry disease and Gaucher disease [Ed1d0a38][Ef06dde0].

A paper reports that Gaucher disease is caused by deficiency of the enzyme glucocerebrosidase, required for the degradation of glycosphingolipids [Ec8d1187]. A paper reports that Fabry disease results from deficient activity of the enzyme alpha-galactosidase A and progressive lysosomal deposition of globotriaosylceramide in cells throughout the body [E871c351]. Because both diseases share this pattern of lysosomal enzyme deficiency and glycosphingolipid storage, I believe there may be useful common ground between our communities, both on the Gaucher side you already support and on the broader lysosomal disease experience your association covers.

Would you be open to a short introductory call in the coming weeks to explore whether there are ways our groups could learn from and support one another?

Thank you for considering this, and I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Maria
Patient group leader (Gaucher)

A paper reports that MLD is a lysosomal storage disorder in which deficient arylsulfatase A activity leads to sulfatide accumulation and demyelination [Ef63ba6a]. A paper reports that Krabbe disease similarly results from a deficiency in the lysosomal enzyme galactocerebrosidase [E050a41e]. A paper also reports that Krabbe disease is characterized by loss and disorganization of myelin [E8b1c4df]. Given these shared features between our two conditions, we believe there may be value for our patient communities in learning from one another, even though Krabbe UK's focus is Krabbe rather than MLD.

Would Krabbe UK be open to a short introductory call to explore whether there are useful ways our two groups could connect or share experiences?

Thank you for considering this, and I look forward to hearing from you.

Maria

Given our shared focus on Tay-Sachs and the related biology across these conditions, I think there could be real value in connecting our communities, whether through sharing resources, coordinating outreach, or simply learning from each other's experience.

Would you be open to a short call, perhaps 20 minutes, to discuss whether a collaboration between our organizations might make sense?

Thank you for considering this. I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
